title: Pain assessment

sources.use: Open RN Nursing Fundamentals (CC BY): landing and TOC only
narrative review of pain evaluation in non-verbal critical care patients (CC BY)

objectives: Assess pain routinely with the unit's tool and reassess after interventions.
Treat pain before considering a sedative.

items.text: Assess pain routinely and before and after painful procedures.
Treat pain before considering a sedative (SCCM good-practice statement).

Document with the unit's tool and reassess after any intervention; use an assessment-driven, protocol-based, stepwise approach where the unit has one (SCCM suggestion, moderate certainty) and titrate only within the protocol.
Analgesic choice and dosing are prescriber or protocol decisions and are not given in this library.
For patients who cannot self-report, behavioural tools are used; item descriptors and thresholds are not reproduced here.
SCCM suggests massage and music therapy may be offered (conditional, low certainty) and suggests not offering virtual reality or hypnosis (conditional, very low).
Reassess after every intervention and before and after painful procedures.
Report uncontrolled or escalating pain to the prescriber.
Record tool, score, interventions and response per your unit's documentation standard.

checklist.text: Use the unit's validated pain tool, including a behavioural tool if the patient cannot self-report.
Assess before and after painful procedures.
Treat pain before considering a sedative, within the protocol.
Offer non-drug measures your policy allows.
Report uncontrolled pain to the prescriber.

gaps: CPOT and BPS descriptors and thresholds, analgesic dosing, regional analgesia: not covered.
PADIS full text: recommendation statements only.
